A map: layers in groups, texts, base maps and palettes

Source: R/map.R
rr_map.Rd

The map is a page with a sidebar of groups that fold, each layer with its info and, when ticked, its controls and legend under it; base maps to choose from; the whole view in the page's address, so a link gives the same view; and on a phone the sidebar behind a menu button. rr_serve() serves it.

Usage

rr_map(
  ...,
  title = "Map",
  view = list(center = c(0, 0), zoom = 2),
  texts = list(),
  languages = "en",
  language = languages[1],
  locales = NULL,
  about = NULL,
  choose = NULL,
  sections = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  palettes = rr_palettes(),
  basemaps = rr_basemaps()
)

Arguments

...

rr_section()s; or, alone, the data a map starts from (a parquet file, folder or glob, a lazy DuckDB table, a data frame or an sf object), which the layer functions (rr_point() and the others) draw.

title

The page's title: a key of texts, or the text itself.

view

The first view: center (longitude, latitude) and zoom.

texts

The texts of the layers and groups, and of the page in other languages: a named list whose elements are a text, or a list of texts by language (list(en = "Ports", is = "Hafnir")). The page's own texts are English; give them in another language under the same keys, a base map's label under b_<id>.

languages

The languages of the page, in the order of its language buttons (none for one language).

language

The language the page opens in.

locales

A list by language of the locales its numbers are written in, the first a browser has (list(is = c("is-IS", "de-DE")), German standing in where a browser lacks Icelandic).

about

Keys of texts for the paragraphs of the About group (none, no group).

choose

Fields whose values the page offers to show, over every layer that has the field (each a control above the groups, with buttons that step through the values): a list with fields, each a field, a label, multi (TRUE: each value a chip ticked on and off, so several show at once; else a list, "all" first, to show one at a time), its options (each a value for the control and the address, a label, match, the value the layers' features carry, NULL for none, and optionally bbox, the extent the view is fitted to, and base, the id of a base map shown while this value is the one chosen: a chart's scale chosen with that chart beneath) and layers (the ids it filters); or, for a range, range ("number", "date" or "time"), closed and its bins (each a lo and a hi as the features carry them, from and to as written, n and optionally bbox); and optionally extents, each a key (each field's value, or a range's bin from 0, joined by the character 31), n and a bbox, by which the fields are linked and the view fitted. rr_map() makes it from the columns its choose names. A choice goes into the address under the field's name, several values separated by commas, a range as from..to, and nothing is fetched again. For a map started from data, its columns written bare, choose = c(id, year), made from the data and linked: text, a factor, a logical or a whole number (an id, a code, a year as an integer) is a list of its values (chips for up to 12); a fraction, a date or a time is a range with two handles, over each of its values where it has at most 64, else over bins between pretty() breaks. Where the data's dictionary (data-dict.tidyverse.org's, in the parquet file's metadata) gives a column's type, it decides: number(id), enum, string or boolean a list, number, number(quantity), date or datetime a range. A path is split by a range's bins, so a choice shows whole runs.

sections

For a map started from data, the sidebar's boxes the layers name (their section), each a title and whether it is open: list(Reference = list(open = FALSE)).

palette

The grid's palette when the page opens: an id of palettes.

palettes, basemaps

The palettes and base maps to choose from: rr_palettes(), rr_basemaps(). The grid offers the palettes for its use (use holding "grid", or no use); a dem layer's colour offers its own list (colour$palettes of rr_layer()), by default the seven looks for a depth. A palette given again under an id replaces the earlier in its place, so c(rr_palettes(), mine) may redefine one.

Value

An rr_map: config (what the page is sent) and layers.

Details

Given data first, rr_map(data) starts a map that the layer functions add to (rr_point() and the others), the data the layers' unless a layer brings its own.

Examples

harbours <- rr_layer(
  "harbours", "vector", label = "Harbours",
  tiles = function(z, x, y) raw(0),
  style = list(list(id = "harbours-fill", type = "fill", "source-layer" = "features",
                    paint = list("fill-color" = "#d9822b")))
)
m <- rr_map(rr_section("ref", "Reference", list(harbours)), title = "Example",
            view = list(center = c(12.5, 56), zoom = 7))
names(m$config)
#> [1] "title"     "view"      "languages" "language"  "groups"    "layers"   
#> [7] "basemaps"  "palettes"  "texts"
